Redirect URI and client are validated before any redirect; earlier failures answer 400 directly and never redirect
RFC 8707 resource binding: authorization and token requests carrying a different resource are rejected and verification rejects tokens for any other resource
RFC 7591 dynamic client registration for public clients only, with bounded input, no client secret and no fetch of client-supplied URLs
RFC 8414 and RFC 9728 metadata derived from a fixed configured issuer, never from request Host headers
Scopes are bounded by a configured ceiling; requests may narrow it and approvals may narrow the request but never widen it
Consent records and authorization codes are single use and consumed atomically; a code is burned on any subsequent mismatch
Access tokens are opaque random secrets stored only as SHA-256 digests with mandatory expiry; revocation is checked on every verification
Verification fails closed on storage error, unknown, revoked, expired or resource-mismatched tokens
Approval requires an application-supplied subject and binding so the product can enforce live ownership on every request
Refresh tokens rotate atomically, never extend the absolute grant lifetime, and reuse by the bound client revokes the whole token family; verification checks grant revocation on every request
